Get data or analyses from audioBlast

Source: R/audioblast.R
audioblast.Rd

Search for data or analyses on audioBlast.

Usage

audioblast(
  type,
  name,
  endpoint = NULL,
  check = TRUE,
  max_pages = NULL,
  page = 1,
  page_size = 50,
  quiet = FALSE,
  on.issue = stop,
  output = "data.frame",
  ...
)

Arguments

type

One of data, analysis, standalone.

name

Name of data or analysis source.

endpoint

Optionally specify endpoint of an audioBlast module.

check

Logical. Checks that the module and endpoint exist before sending the query to audioBlast.

max_pages

Maximum number of data pages to return, by default this is set to NULL and returns all pages.

page

First page of results to request, defaults to 1.

page_size

Number of results on each page, defaults to 50. Larger pages need fewer requests to fetch many results.

quiet

If true will not print progress. Silence is a virtue.

on.issue

Function to call on error or warning. By default stop to raise a standard R error. Setting to warning will instead a warning.

output

By default a data.frame. "Annotations" will return a list of Annotation objects. "JSON-LD" and "Turtle" return the RDF that audioBlast gives for modules that describe their records as linked data, as a character vector with one element for each page.

...

Fields and values to filter on. Any field defined by audioBlast.

Value

A data frame, a list of Annotation objects or a character vector, depending on output. NULL if nothing matches the query.

Details

Filters are given as named arguments in .... audioBlast refuses a filter that a module does not have with an error naming it, and audioblastFilters() lists the filters a module has.

A filter that audioBlast lists as taking several values can be given a vector, e.g. id = c(10754, 11096), which matches a row holding any one of them. audioBlast takes at most 100 values in a request, so longer vectors are sent as several requests and their results combined.

A filter on a range (e.g. duration or lat) can be given a single value, matched exactly, or a range made with ab_range(), e.g. duration = ab_range(10, 20).

Columns that audioBlast describes as numeric are returned as numbers, and all others as character strings.

See also

audioblastFilters() for the filters a module takes, audioblastRecord() to fetch one record, and audioblastDownload() to download the recordings found.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
audioblast("data", "recordings", taxon="Gryllotalpa vineae")

# Several recordings at once
audioblast("data", "recordings", source="bio.acousti.ca", id=c(10754, 11096))

# Recordings between 10 and 20 seconds long
audioblast("data", "recordings", source="bio.acousti.ca",
           duration=ab_range(10, 20), max_pages=1)

# The classification of a taxon, from the root down
audioblast("data", "taxa", "classification", source="bio.acousti.ca", id=247)
} # }
